title: LittleBit-2: Maximizing the Spectral Energy Gain in Sub-1-Bit LLMs via Latent Geometry Alignment
claim: Standard factorization yields spiky, axis-aligned latents that mismatch binary targets; rotating them onto hypercube diagonals minimizes quantization error.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, central arrow labeled with the transformation
description: Two side-by-side 2-D coordinate plots, with axes u1 and u2 and black square markers at the four binary target corners (±1, ±1). Left panel (a), in blue and titled 'LittleBit (Standard SVD)', shows two overlapping elongated ellipses along the axes. Solid arrows point along the axes, and a dashed line to the nearest corner is labeled 'Large Error'. A small inset shows a single spiky, zero-centered peak. A thick orange arrow in the middle is labeled 'Internal Rotation (Joint-ITQ)' and 'Geometry Alignment'. Right panel (b), in red and titled 'LittleBit-2 (Ours)', shows a four-lobed clover-shaped distribution. Its arrows are rotated onto the diagonals and end at the corner markers, labeled 'Min Error'. The inset shows a bimodal distribution marked 'Margin ↑'. Blue versus red contrast draws the eye first.
caption: Latent Geometry Alignment. (a) Standard singular vectors exhibit high coherence (spiky distribution), clustering along the axes. This creates a geometric mismatch with the binary quantization targets (black dots at (±1, ±1)). (b) LittleBit-2 employs Internal Latent Rotation via Joint-ITQ. Acting as a geometric preconditioner, it rotates latent factors to align with binary hypercube diagonals. This minimizes quantization noise (min error) and maximizes the optimization margin (Bimodal distribution).
abstract: We identify the Spectral Energy Gain in extreme model compression, where low-rank binary approximations outperform tiny-rank floating-point baselines for heavy-tailed spectra. However, prior attempts fail to realize this potential, trailing state-of-the-art 1-bit methods. We attribute this degradation to Latent Geometry Misalignment: standard singular vectors exhibit high coherence (spiky distribution), the worst-case geometry for binary quantization. To realize this gain, we propose LittleBit-2, a framework employing Internal Latent Rotation and Joint Iterative Quantization (Joint-ITQ). This approach acts as a geometric preconditioner, aligning coherent latent distributions with the binary hypercube with zero inference overhead. Empirically, LittleBit-2 establishes a new state-of-the-art in the sub-1-bit regime (1$\sim$0.1 bpp) on Llama-2 and Llama-3, matching the fidelity of leading 1-bit baselines.
